title: It was raining
goal: Set the scene of a story and describe an interrupted action with the past continuous -(I)yordu.

intro.text: Put `-DI` after `-(I)yor` to say what was going on: *yağıyor* (it is raining) → *yağıyordu* (it was raining). Use it for the background of a story, and for an action that something else interrupted: *Kitap okuyordum, telefon çaldı.*

exercises.question: How do you say **It was raining**?

why.1: *Yağdı* reports an event, **it rained**; it doesn't set a scene.
why.3: *-m* is the ending for **I**: **I was raining**.

exercises.explain: `-(I)yor` + *-du*: *yağıyordu*, **it was raining**, the background of a scene.

exercises.label: *çalışmak* (to work) in the past continuous: I was working, you were working…
exercises.explain: *-yordu* never changes: the u of *-yor* sets the vowel, and r is voiced, so d. Then the past endings *-m, -n, -k, -nuz*.

exercises.text: Dün akşam saat sekizde ne yap___?
exercises.en: What were you doing at eight o'clock yesterday evening?

reject.why: *Ne yaptın?* asks what you did. **Were doing** needs *-ıyordun*.

exercises.hint: **Were you doing**: present continuous + past + the ending for **you**.

exercises.prompt: Güneş parlıyordu ve hafif bir rüzgâr esiyordu.
accept: The sun was shining and a light wind was blowing.
The sun was shining and a [gentle|soft] [wind|breeze] was blowing.
The sun was shining and a light breeze was blowing.
The sun was shining and there was a [light|gentle] [wind|breeze].

exercises.en: I was reading a book, Ali was sleeping.

exercises.prompt: I was reading a book when the phone rang.

reject.why: *Okudum* says you read it, full stop. The reading was going on when the phone rang: *okuyordum*.

exercises.prompt: It was snowing and the children were playing in the garden.
exercises.text: Kar yağıyordu ve çocuklar bahçede oynuyordu.
accept: Kar yağıyordu ve çocuklar bahçede oynuyorlardı.

exercises.explain: The e of *bekle-* drops before `-(I)yor`, as in the present: *bekliyor*. After *-yor* the past is always *-du*.

exercises.question: Which sentence sets the scene, rather than telling what happened?

why.1: *Çıktı* is an event: **the sun came out**.

exercises.explain: Scenes and backgrounds are in `-(I)yordu`: *Güneş parlıyordu*, **the sun was shining**.

exercises.prompt: It was raining at night, and we got wet.
accept: Gece yağmur yağıyordu ve biz ıslandık.
Gece yağmur yağıyordu, biz de ıslandık.

reject.why: *Yağdı* is an event of its own. **Was raining** is the scene in which you got wet: *yağıyordu*.

exercises.text: O sırada ben mutfakta yemek ___, Ayşe salonda müzik dinliyordu.
exercises.en: At that moment I was cooking in the kitchen, and Ayşe was listening to music in the living room.
exercises.explain: *O sırada* freezes a scene in progress, so both verbs are in `-(I)yordu`: *yapıyordum*, *dinliyordu*.
